definitions.definition: ell=max(λ,0), regarded as a natural number (the integer-to-natural conversion λ.toNat). This definition imposes no range condition on λ.
J=Fin(ell+1), identified with the integers i satisfying 0≤i≤ell.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, X_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ x^r, with x^0=Id_V. Factorials are the usual products, with 0!=1.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, Y_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ y^r, with y^0=Id_V.
For i∈J set e_i=Y_i(v)=y^i(v)/i!; the index i denotes its natural value.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(ℂ)
definitions.definition: U_ℤ is generated over ℤ by the divided powers x^r/r! and y^r/r! for all natural r. Its action on V is generated by the operators X_r,Y_r. Operator stability under this algebra means stability under every generator.

definitions.type: sequence of integer-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For every natural r, A_r=X_r|M, the restriction to M. Its construction requires the original admissibility hypothesis that every X_r preserves M. In particular A_1=x|M and A_0=Id_M.

definitions.type: sequence of integer-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For every natural r, B_r=Y_r|M, the restriction to M. Its construction requires the original admissibility hypothesis that every Y_r preserves M. In particular B_1=y|M and B_0=Id_M.
For i,j∈J let s_ij=j!(ell−j)! A_(ell−i) B_ell A_ell B_(ell−j), with integer scalar multiplication. Products of endomorphisms mean composition with the right factor first.

inputs.statement: Let p be any prime, K any field of characteristic p, λ an integer with 0≤λ<p, V=V(λ) the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂-module of dimension λ+1, and x,y,h its Chevalley operators satisfying hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h. Let v∈V be nonzero with xv=0 and hv=λv. Let U_ℤ be the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r!, r≥0. Let M⊆V be any U_ℤ-stable free abelian subgroup with an integer basis also a complex basis of V. The target space is M⊗_ℤ K with the induced x,y,h actions and the Chevalley Lie algebra (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, including characteristic two.

The family (e_i)_(i∈J) is a complex basis of V. For every natural r and i∈J, X_r e_i=binom(ell−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and equals zero if r>i; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤ell and equals zero if i+r>ell. All binomial coefficients in these formulas are natural binomial coefficients mapped to ℂ. The subscript of an e vector is used only in the branch in which it lies in J.

output.statement: Every s_ij is an integer-linear endomorphism of the original lattice M. For all i,j,k,l∈J, s_ij s_kl=δ_jk ell! s_il, and ∑_(i∈J) s_ii=ell! Id_M, where δ_jk is 1 when j=k and 0 otherwise. For every natural r, r! A_r=(A_1)^r and r! B_r=(B_1)^r in End_ℤ(M). More precisely, in the complex basis e, the complex operator j!(ell−j)! X_(ell−i)Y_ell X_ell Y_(ell−j) sends e_k to ell! e_i if k=j and to zero otherwise, and its restriction to M is s_ij.

locals.declaration: Define Emat_ij on the basis e by Emat_ij(e_k)=e_i if k=j and zero otherwise.
Set P0=Y_ell X_ell, with right-first composition.

argument.text: Since N001 makes e a basis, define Emat_ij by its displayed basis action, extended complex-linearly. Put P0=Y_ell X_ell. For k<ell, N001 gives X_ell e_k=0. For k=ell, X_ell e_ell=e_0 and Y_ell e_0=e_ell, both with coefficient 1. Hence P0=Emat_(ell,ell). N001 also gives X_(ell−i)e_ell=e_i, so X_(ell−i)P0=Emat_(i,ell) for every i∈J. Equality on basis vectors implies equality of operators.

produces.statement: P0=Emat_(ell,ell), and for every i∈J, X_(ell−i)P0=Emat_(i,ell).

argument.text: For j,k∈J evaluate P0 Y_(ell−j)e_k using N001. If k<j the resulting index k+ell−j is below ell and P0 kills it. If k>j it exceeds ell and Y_(ell−j)e_k=0. If k=j, the result is binom(ell,ell−j)e_ell=binom(ell,j)e_ell. Thus P0 Y_(ell−j)=binom(ell,j)Emat_(ell,j). Define Tmat_ij=X_(ell−i)P0 Y_(ell−j). By F001 it is binom(ell,j)Emat_ij. The factorial identity j!(ell−j)! binom(ell,j)=ell! therefore gives j!(ell−j)! Tmat_ij=ell! Emat_ij for all i,j. This establishes precisely the asserted complex action in the asserted output.

produces.statement: For every i,j∈J, j!(ell−j)! Tmat_ij=ell! Emat_ij as complex operators; Tmat_ij=X_(ell−i)Y_ell X_ell Y_(ell−j).

argument.text: By H001 every X_r and Y_r preserves M and is ℤ-linear on restriction. Compositions and multiplication by the integer j!(ell−j)! preserve M, so D011 defines s_ij as the restriction of the complex operator in F002. Direct evaluation on e gives Emat_ij Emat_kl=δ_jk Emat_il and ∑_i Emat_ii=Id_V. Consequently F002 gives the products of the scaled operators equal to δ_jk ell! times the corresponding scaled operator, and their diagonal sum equal to ell! Id_V. Restrict these equalities to M. Equality of their values in V implies equality in M because M is a submodule with injective inclusion. This proves the two identities claimed for s in End_ℤ(M).

For any natural r, r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r on V by their definitions and the nonzero complex factorial. On M the restriction of x^r is (A_1)^r, as follows by induction from A_1=x|M and x(M)⊆M; similarly for y and B_1. Restriction and the injective inclusion give r! A_r=(A_1)^r and r! B_r=(B_1)^r for every r. Together with S003 and the exact action in F002 this proves all of the asserted output. At ell=0 every product and factorial used above has its empty-product value 1.
